text:
For most UK sole traders and small businesses, **Starling is my best all-round starting point**: no monthly fee, no fees on UK bank transfers, and accounting integrations. Cash deposits at the Post Office cost **0.7% (minimum £3)**, so it’s less attractive if you regularly bank cash. 〔Starling〕(https://www.starlingbank.com/business-account/)

Other good fits:

- **Mettle** — worth a look if you’re a sole trader or a small business with up to two owners and want simple free banking. It offers invoicing and, for eligible users, FreeAgent accounting. Check its eligibility and cash-deposit fees before applying. 〔Mettle overview〕(https://www.money.co.uk/business-bank-accounts/pm-1)
- **Monzo Business Lite** — a good option if you prefer managing everything in an app; UK transfers are free, and cash deposits cost £1 each, subject to limits. 〔Comparison〕(https://www.businessexpert.co.uk/business-banking/best-business-accounts/)
- **Tide** — useful if you want invoicing and business admin tools in one place, but check transaction limits: its free plan includes only a limited number of free transfers, then charges per transfer. 〔Tide pricing〕(https://www.tide.co/pricing/)
- **A high-street bank** — consider HSBC, NatWest, Lloyds or Virgin Money if branch access or in-person cash handling matters more than having the simplest app-based account. Introductory offers and ongoing fees vary. 〔Comparison〕(https://www.moneysavingexpert.com/banking/business-bank-account/)

**Quick rule of thumb:** mainly UK transfers and little cash → Starling; want app-based banking → Monzo; want built-in admin or accounting → compare Mettle and Tide; need branch services → check high-street options.

Sole traders aren’t generally required by law to have a separate business account, but banks’ personal-account terms may restrict business use. Limited companies should use a business account. Compare the current fees, eligibility, cash limits and deposit protection directly with the provider before deciding, as these can change.
